base_instruction: You are a helpful catering and event planning assistant. Help the user plan food for a memorial service reception. Track who is attending, their dietary needs, and any logistical details. When the user asks you to evaluate specific menu items, check each item against every active attendee's current dietary constraints.

state_queue.anchor: Hi, I need some help planning the food for my grandmother's memorial service reception this Saturday. It's going to be at the community hall after the service.

flow_info.value: Core family attending: me, my mom, my Uncle Richard, and my Aunt Patty
Mom was diagnosed with celiac disease a couple years ago
Uncle Richard had a triple bypass surgery six months ago, his doctor has him on a strict low-sodium diet
Aunt Patty ate shrimp at a wedding last year and her throat started closing up, she had to use an EpiPen
We're expecting about 30 people total, but these four plus me are the ones I need to make sure are covered
We're trying to keep it around $12-15 per person, so maybe $400 total for food
My cousin Maya just confirmed she's flying in from Portland, she'll be there too

Uncle Richard just called — he's still recovering and his doctor doesn't want him standing around for hours, so he's only coming to the church service, not the reception. But he asked if I could set aside a plate for him to take home
Aunt Patty texted me — turns out after more allergy testing, it's not just shrimp, her allergist said she's allergic to all shellfish

Mom told me she went back to her gastroenterologist and they re-ran the biopsy — turns out she was misdiagnosed, she doesn't actually have celiac. She's been eating bread again for weeks with no issues

The deli down the street gave me a catering quote. Their memorial reception package includes: ham and cheese pinwheel sandwiches, a mixed green salad with balsamic vinaigrette, New England clam chowder, a fruit and cheese platter, and lemon bars. Does this work?

constraints.value: Cannot eat gluten — no wheat, barley, rye, or products containing them
constraints.surface_form: Mom was diagnosed with celiac disease a couple years ago
inference_chain: Celiac disease → autoimmune reaction to gluten
Gluten → found in wheat, barley, rye
Must avoid bread, pasta, most baked goods, many sauces

constraints.value: Must eat low-sodium food — no cured meats, salty soups, heavily seasoned items
constraints.surface_form: Uncle Richard had a triple bypass surgery six months ago, his doctor has him on a strict low-sodium diet

constraints.value: Cannot eat any shellfish — shrimp, crab, lobster, clams, mussels, oysters, etc.
constraints.surface_form: Aunt Patty ate shrimp at a wedding last year and her throat started closing up, she had to use an EpiPen
inference_chain: Anaphylactic reaction to shrimp → shrimp allergy
Later confirmed: allergic to all shellfish (constraint upgraded from shrimp-only)

constraints.value: Cannot eat meat, fish, eggs, or root vegetables (onions, garlic, potatoes, carrots)
constraints.surface_form: Cousin Maya has been practicing Jain for about three years now, takes it pretty seriously
inference_chain: Practicing Jain → follows Jain dietary laws
Jain diet → no meat, no fish, no eggs
Strict Jain → also no root vegetables (onions, garlic, potatoes, carrots)

hidden_state.value: You are planning food for your grandmother's memorial service reception. You will introduce family members and their health situations across several turns. Plans will change — people will join, leave, and medical situations will be updated. At the end, you will share a specific catering menu and ask if it works. You must NEVER hint at which items are problematic or mention specific dietary rules — just share the menu and ask.

You are a calm, matter-of-fact person handling family logistics during a difficult time. You relay updates from family members in third person ('Mom told me...', 'Uncle Richard called and said...'). You never express frustration or impatience with the changing plans — it's just how family events go. You are slightly subdued given the occasion but not emotional.
hidden_state.description: Prevents emotion escalation and ensures third-person relay for family updates

ground_truth.answer: Ham and cheese pinwheel sandwiches: problematic for cousin Maya (Jain — no meat; ham is meat). Also problematic for Uncle Richard's take-home plate (ham is cured meat, very high sodium). New England clam chowder: problematic for Aunt Patty (clams are shellfish — confirmed shellfish allergy). Also problematic for cousin Maya (Jain — clam chowder contains animal product). Also problematic for Uncle Richard's take-home plate (chowder is typically high sodium). Mixed green salad with balsamic vinaigrette: fine for the reception table, but agent should note it may contain onion/garlic which would be an issue for Maya if included (Jain — no root vegetables). Fruit and cheese platter: fine for everyone at the reception. Fine for Uncle Richard's take-home plate (fruit and cheese are naturally low-sodium). Lemon bars: fine for everyone — Mom's celiac was a misdiagnosis so gluten is no longer an issue. Maya can eat lemon bars (no meat/fish/eggs/root vegetables in standard lemon bars, though agent should note eggs may be an ingredient in lemon bars which would affect Maya).
required_elements: Ham and cheese pinwheel sandwiches are problematic for cousin Maya because ham is meat and she follows a Jain diet
New England clam chowder is problematic for Aunt Patty because clams are shellfish and she has a confirmed shellfish allergy
New England clam chowder is also problematic for cousin Maya because it contains animal product, incompatible with Jain diet
Ham and cheese pinwheel sandwiches should not go on Uncle Richard's take-home plate because ham is cured meat and high in sodium
New England clam chowder should not go on Uncle Richard's take-home plate because chowder is typically high in sodium
Lemon bars are fine — agent does NOT flag them for gluten or celiac because Mom's celiac was a misdiagnosis and has been resolved
forbidden_elements: Flagging any item as problematic for Mom due to celiac or gluten — her celiac was a misdiagnosis and is resolved
Saying Aunt Patty is only allergic to shrimp — her allergy was upgraded to all shellfish
Flagging items as problematic for Uncle Richard at the reception table — he is not attending the reception, only needs a take-home plate
Saying the fruit and cheese platter is problematic for anyone currently attending the reception
Over-generalizing Aunt Patty's shellfish allergy to all seafood — fish is not shellfish
ground_truth.explanation: This scenario tests entity lifecycle tracking and inferential constraint reasoning across a memorial service reception planning conversation. The agent must track: (1) Mom's celiac constraint is REMOVED mid-conversation (misdiagnosis resolved — she can eat gluten again), (2) Uncle Richard EXITS the reception but needs a take-home plate (his low-sodium constraint shifts from reception to take-home scope only), (3) Aunt Patty's allergy is UPGRADED from shrimp-only to all shellfish, (4) Cousin Maya JOINS late with a high-constraint Jain diet (no meat, no fish, no eggs, no root vegetables — inferential chain from 'practicing Jain'). At probe time, the 5 menu items produce mixed verdicts: ham pinwheels are clearly problematic (Maya: meat; Uncle Richard take-home: high sodium cured meat), clam chowder is clearly problematic (Aunt Patty: shellfish; Maya: animal product; Uncle Richard take-home: high sodium), mixed green salad is mostly fine but has a nuance (root vegetables for Maya depending on ingredients), fruit and cheese platter is fine for everyone, and lemon bars are a trap — they look problematic for Mom (contain flour/gluten) but her celiac was resolved so they are fine. The over-generalization trap is Aunt Patty: shellfish allergy does NOT mean all seafood allergy.

mechanism: Late-joiner with high-constraint: new person with strict needs arrives late
